name: Links
purpose: Text links (browser) — let users navigate between pages/content items or instigate actions (e.g. 'download pdf', 'open in a new window'). Family of four: Arrow link (chevron after text), Back link (chevron before text), Icon link (leading icon), Inline link (within body copy). Each on-light + on-dark.
$family: Covers the Links canvas; each type is a separate Figma component. Page title: 'Text links (browser)'.

props.name: multiline
props.$note: Arrow link supports multiline (chevron stays attached to last word).

variants.name: arrow
variants.use: Chevron trails the text. font-1…7. Arrow icon is BRAND RED on light (color/primary), white on dark. Uses font-N/regular-link (font 1-4) + font-5/6/7 medium-link. Chevron is EM-SCALED (width/height:.85em) + FLEX-CENTRED (align-items:center; gap:4px) so it tracks the type size and needs no fixed-px sizing. (2026-07-17: retired the legacy icon/arrow/font-N + padding/arrow/font-N fixed-px scheme — parked in tokens/_icon-scale-hsbc-general.json + _spacing-hsbc-general.json.)

variants.name: back
variants.use: Chevron precedes the text (back navigation). font-5/6/7 medium-link. Back arrow is NEUTRAL (icon/default), not red.

variants.name: icon
variants.use: Leading icon + label, fixed-size S5/S6/S7. Only type with an explicit disabled state. Icon + text neutral (icon/default + text/default).

variants.name: inline
variants.use: Link set within running body text. font-5 LIGHT weight (font-5/light-link) to sit in paragraph flow; default + hover/pressed only.

arrow.sizing: em-scaled chevron: .tip svg width/height .85em, flex-centred (align-items:center; gap:4px) — scales with type, no fixed-px icon/padding tokens

tokens.$rebind-finding: (2026-06-19) arrow-icon binds the color/primary PRIMITIVE; rebind to semantic primary/background/default. Links distinguished by underline not colour (1.4.1); keyboard focus = thickened underline (:focus-visible) in text/default, not a blue ring.

responsive.$status: PROMOTED 2026-06-24 (Dave) — closes Dim 11 to reach prototype-grade 9/9.
responsive.rule: Single links are intrinsically fluid (inline links wrap with the text). The responsive unit is a LINK LIST (related-links / footer / utility nav): row + wrap on a wide container; when narrow it stacks.
responsive.breakpoint: container <= 420px (container-query on the list, not a viewport media query; verified to 320px / WCAG 1.4.10, 0 horizontal overflow).
responsive.stacked: List items stack vertically and each link gets block display + vertical padding so its tap target is adequate when not in a text run (WCAG 2.5.8).
responsive.$note: States also extended at promotion: :active mirrors :hover (the meta's combined hover/pressed state), and aria-current="page" marks the current link in a list — distinguished by weight + persistent thick underline, never colour alone (1.4.1). Icon-link family member added to canon (homes the disabled state); its glyph is the real library download.svg via a sprite. Built/verified in _fitness-test/links-responsive.html.

accessibility.distinguishable: Links must be distinguishable from body text by more than colour (underline/affordance) — esp. inline links (1.4.1)
accessibility.states: hover and pressed are a single combined state; ensure focus-visible is present and state change is not colour-only (same WCAG state-contrast flag as Breadcrumbs)
accessibility.linkPurpose: Link text should describe the destination/action (avoid 'click here'); arrow/back chevrons are decorative and must not be the only label
accessibility.arrowContrast: Arrow link's red arrow (color/primary #db0011) on white passes; on dark the arrow is white
accessibility.iconLayout: Back/Icon link icons sit left, aligned to the FIRST line of text (not vertically centred); arrow chevron stays attached to the last word, never on its own line
accessibility.targetArea: Inline/text links should still offer an adequate hit/touch area

antiPatterns: Letting the arrow chevron fall onto its own line — it must always be accompanied by a word
Positioning the back/icon glyph vertically centred between lines instead of aligned to the first line
Providing so many links that the path becomes unclear or distracts from the task
Distinguishing inline links by colour alone (no underline/affordance)
Leaving Icon link on-dark hover/disabled bound to the deprecated on-dark tokens — rebind hover to icon/default-reverse + text/reverse; on-dark disabled has NO live equivalent (see tokenValidation)

tokenValidation.against: token store re-based on Figma native variable export
tokenValidation.result: PASS — Arrow/Back/Inline + Icon (on-light) clean; Icon link ON-DARK carries 4 deprecated tokens (2 clean rebinds, 2 no-equivalent blockers)
tokenValidation.primitiveBinding: Arrow link's arrow icon binds the PRIMITIVE color/primary (#db0011) directly rather than a semantic icon token — same pattern flagged on Badge surface and Hero arrow/CTA. Consider a semantic 'icon/brand' token.

tokens.rebind: REVIEW — NO live equivalent (same blocker as Avatar on-dark disabled)

depricateUsage.note: KEY FINDING: the on-dark disabled blocker tokens (#767676), previously seen ONLY on Avatar, are ALSO used here by Icon link. This is no longer an Avatar-only edge case — a live on-dark disabled text/icon token is needed before these depricates can be deleted. The on-dark hover tokens are redundant (#fff = reverse) → clean. On-light disabled is already migrated (icon/disabled + text/disabled).

edges.$obeys-contract: AUTHORED, not inferred (P-274-3 + s275-D5, lane TO #276). `rule:` refs are joined by FILENAME from knowledge/guidelines/_rules-index.json — never by a regex over rule prose. `ux:` refs are the six grade-A laws s269-D5 names. Each $why is one line, written by reading the rule and this meta together, reviewed by eye. PROPOSED — not ratified.

obeys.$why: States what a Link IS against a Button — primarily navigation, lower-priority or many same-priority actions — which is this meta's `purpose` sentence.
Don't provide so many links that it is unclear where to go — a density constraint on this molecule in context.
Chevron links carry a RED chevron as signposting — fixes the glyph and colour of one of the meta's four family members.
Back links put the chevron on the LEFT pointing left — the Back link member of the family of four.
Arrow sizing is numeric and font-tier-keyed (x-height or cap-height, gap = arrow/2) — the Arrow link's geometry, tied to the type scale this meta already binds.
Wrap behaviour differs by type: the arrow stays attached to the last word, the back/icon glyph stays aligned to the first line — per-member layout behaviour.
Only globally recognised icons, per the icons guidelines — constrains the Icon link member's slot.
Download links: icon on the LEFT plus file format and size in brackets — the meta's own purpose names 'download pdf' as a link job.
External links open in a new tab with the indicator icon at the END, as PART of the link — fixes both behaviour and anatomy.
Underlined within body text, weight MATCHES the surrounding text in all states — binds this molecule's type tokens to its container's.
Hyperlink ≤5 words, descriptive of the destination, preferably at the end of the sentence — content contract for the inline member.
Internal links open in the current tab, external in a new tab — the behaviour half of the external-link rule, stated for both cases.
Hover underlines on mouse-over of text OR icon and the target wraps both — icon and text are ONE link, which is a composition fact about this molecule.
On dark, links and their icons are white — the per-theme token binding this meta's `tokens` block has to satisfy.
Link text describes the action or destination, sentence case, ≤8 words, no 'Click here', no full stop — the content contract across the family.

CROSS-FILE, authored: the buttons spec draws the boundary from the other side — 'for less prominent actions, we use text links'. It binds Links as much as Button, and is the only rule in this set that does not come from common-toolkit-links.md.
ctkl-018 wraps the target area around icon AND text as one link — a deliberate enlargement of a small inline target.
ctkl-002 ('don't provide so many links it becomes unclear where to go') is Hick stated as a Don't.
ctkl-015/ctkl-022 cap link text and demand it describe the destination: a scannable link is fast, and a vague one is fast AND wrong.
